item.title: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
item.description:
By Raphael Satter

WASHINGTON, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.

item.title: EU and Gulf states postpone summit due in Saudi Arabia
item.description:
By Timour Azhari

RIYADH/BRUSSELS, Oct 15 (Reuters) - The European Union and Gulf states on Thursday postponed a joint summit due to be held in Saudi Arabia next week, as sustained attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis fuel concerns about air travel to and from the kingdom.

The Gulf Cooperation Council cited continued Houthi threats against Saudi Arabia and an extended suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport when announcing the postponement of the summit scheduled for October 24 in Riyadh.

item.title: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia could be postponed but 'no hurry' to decide: AFC
item.description:
The Asian Cup scheduled for January in Saudi Arabia could be moved back a year to 2028 "if we need to", the continent's top football official said, following a series of Houthi attacks on the country.

But AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa also said they were in "no hurry" to make a decision over Asia's premier football tournament.

The 2027 Asian Cup is supposed to kick off on January 7 in the Saudi cities of Jeddah, Riyadh and Al Khobar.

item.title: Prolonged war, renewed disruptions pose biggest risk to Middle East region, IMF says
item.description:
By Andrea Shalal

BANGKOK, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Prolonged war in the Middle East and further disruptions to energy production, shipping routes or critical infrastructure pose the biggest risk to economies in the Middle East and Central Asia, the International Monetary Fund said on Thursday.

Jihad Azour, the IMF's director for the Middle East and Central Asia, told reporters the war was imposing a highly uneven economic shock to the broader region, with directly affected states under severe pressure.

item.title: US military weighs use of ‘mother of all bombs’ in potential future strikes on Iran, CNN says
item.description: Oct 15 (Reuters) - The US military has developed strike plans that could include using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, also known as the "mother of all bombs", against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if President Donald Trump orders renewed combat operations, CNN reported on Thursday citing USofficials familiar with the matter.

item.title: Russia's Lavrov, China's Wang discuss cooperation, Ukraine, Iran at Asia security meeting
item.description:
Oct 14 (Reuters) - The Russian and Chinese foreign ministers discussed the state of bilateral cooperation as well as the crises in Ukraine and Iran during an Asia security meeting, the Russian Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.

Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping reaffirmed their strategic alliance at a regional summit last August and both praised prospects for closer cooperation.

item.title: UN peacekeeping chief says talks on future of Lebanon mission must begin soon
item.description:
By Maya Gebeily

BEIRUT, Oct 14 (Reuters) - UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix on Wednesday urged the UN Security Council to begin negotiations on the future of peacekeepers deployed in Lebanon, as Beirut campaigns for an extension to the mandate set to expire at the end of this year.

A UN peacekeeping force known as UNIFIL has been deployedin southern Lebanon since 1978 but the Security Council last year ordered the mission to begin withdrawing at the end of 2026.

item.title: Two ships sink near Hormuz after being hit by projectiles amid surge in attacks
item.description:
By Jonathan Saul and Renee Maltezou

LONDON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - A container ship and a dry bulk carrier have both sunk near the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday.

Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.
